newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain given more time to liberalise telecoms industry.
newsitem.headline: Spain given more time to liberalise telecoms industry.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday agreed to give Spain more time to liberalise its telecoms industry as part of plan for total EU liberalisation of the sector.

A statement by Karel van Miert, European commissioner responsible for competition policy, said Spain would be given until 30 November next year to completely liberalise its voice telephone and public telecoms networks.
Previously, Spain had been obliged to complete the operation by the begining of next year.

The Commission said the additional time granted Spain was entirely compatible with the World Trade Organisation agreement on basic telecommunications reached in February, to which the EU is a signatory.

Under the extension, Spain will have to advise the Commission how it intends to grant licences for voice telephones before the end of the year and publish the procedure as law before August 1988. Licences will have to be granted by December 1 that year.
From next month, Spain will also have to ensure that all restrictions on the supply of already liberalised services are lifted.

Spain also has to ensure that during this year -- under certain conditions -- cable operators are allowed to provide voice telephony and that a third licence for voice telephony is granted by January 1988.

The Commission has already granted extentions to liberalisation timetables to Ireland, Portugal, Luxembourg and Spain. A decision on Greece is still outstanding. -- David Fox, Brussels Newsroom ++ 32 2 287 6832.
